claims.text: The Unwarranted Associations (UA) framework provides a methodology for discovering unfair, discriminatory, or offensive user treatment in data-driven applications.
The UA framework unifies prior attempts at formalizing algorithmic fairness.
FairTest instantiates the Unwarranted Associations (UA) framework to check data-driven applications for unfair user treatment.
FairTest provides debugging capabilities that let programmers rule out potential confounders for observed unfair effects.
FairTest revealed subtle biases against older populations in the distribution of error in a predictive health application.
FairTest revealed offensive racial labeling in an image tagger application.

evidence.description: Application of FairTest to four data-driven applications revealed subtle biases against older populations in the distribution of error in a predictive health application.
Application of FairTest to four data-driven applications revealed offensive racial labeling in an image tagger.

methodologies.name: Unwarranted Associations (UA) framework
methodologies.description: A methodology for discovering unfair, discriminatory, or offensive user treatment by combining investigative primitives, fairness metrics, subgroup exploration, and utility considerations.

methodologies.name: FairTest
methodologies.description: A software tool instantiating the UA framework that enables statistical investigation of associations between application outcomes and sensitive attributes along with confounder debugging.

limitations.text: A lack of appropriate methodologies and tools makes identifying unfair or discriminatory effects challenging in practice.
